_comment: Paste-ready node JSON for the n8n workflow `report_ingest` (id 3NRvDchKPT5RK4tn).
State as of 2026-09-09, after the out-of-memory fix and the rebuild-batching change.
Only the nodes on the ingestion path are here; the error/alert branch and the sticky
TWO INVARIANTS, and both were paid for:
1. ONE report email per execution. `Find Unprocessed Reports` is limit 1. Raising it
reintroduces the crash loop of 2026-09-08 - see AUDIT_PLAN.md A2.
2. dbt rebuilds ONCE PER BURST, not once per report. `Any Reports Left?` asks whether
the inbox still holds a report; if it does this run skips the rebuild and the last
run of the burst pays for it. That is what makes a 2-minute sweep affordable.

nodes.name: Sweep every 2 min
nodes.notes: Every 2 minutes. A run that finds nothing costs ~0.7s and one that lands a report without rebuilding dbt costs ~15s, so frequency is cheap - it is the dbt rebuild that is expensive, and that now runs once per burst.

filters.q: from:no-reply@smartmoving.com subject:"Report is Ready" in:inbox newer_than:7d

nodes.name: Find Unprocessed Reports
nodes.notes: Every report email still in the inbox. Trashing on success is what makes the inbox the queue.

nodes.name: Shape Gmail Like IMAP
nodes.notes: Gmail's shape differs from IMAP's. One adapter here so Resolve Report Metadata stays untouched.

parameters.query:
-- One statement for the whole report. This used to be one INSERT per row, which
-- turned a 5,000-row report into 5,000 round trips - executions ran 20 to 30 minutes
-- and n8n held an item per row for the entire run. Set-based landing is the same
-- write with the same conflict semantics, in one call.
INSERT INTO raw_smartmoving.{{ $json.target_table }}
  (source_instance_id, entity_id, report_generated_at, row_key, row_data, _source_email)
SELECT r.source_instance_id,
       r.entity_id,
       r.report_generated_at::timestamptz,
       r.row_key,
       r.row_data,
       r._source_email
FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) AS r(
  source_instance_id  text,
  entity_id           text,
  report_generated_at text,
  row_key             text,
  row_data            jsonb,
  _source_email       text)
ON CONFLICT (source_instance_id, report_generated_at, row_key) DO NOTHING;

SELECT
  $3::int AS expected_records,
  (SELECT count(*)
     FROM raw_smartmoving.{{ $json.target_table }}
    WHERE source_instance_id  = $1
      AND report_generated_at = $2::timestamptz) AS landed_records

nodes.name: Collect Emails To Clean
nodes.notes: One item per distinct message that landed successfully in this execution.

nodes.name: Find Email In Gmail
nodes.notes: Resolves the RFC822 Message-ID to a Gmail message id. IMAP gives us the header id; the Gmail API needs its own.

nodes.name: Move Email To Trash
nodes.notes: Adds the TRASH label to THIS message only. Never the thread - all reports share one.

nodes.name: Any Reports Left?

filters.q: from:no-reply@smartmoving.com subject:"Report is Ready" in:inbox newer_than:7d

nodes.notes: Is another report still queued? The inbox IS the queue, so one hit means more work is pending and this run should not pay for a dbt rebuild.

nodes.name: Inbox Drained?
nodes.notes: TRUE = nothing left, so rebuild dbt now. FALSE = more reports queued, skip the rebuild and let the last run of the burst pay for it once.

parameters.command: out=$(flock -w 900 /tmp/dw-dbt.lock -c 'cd /home/datawarehouse_user/datawarehouse/dbt && set -a && . /home/datawarehouse_user/datawarehouse/.env && set +a && /home/datawarehouse_user/datawarehouse/venv/bin/dbt build --profiles-dir . --target dev --no-use-colors' 2>&1); rc=$?; echo "$out" | tail -40; exit $rc
